questions.q: What does HumanEval measure, and how is a generated solution actually graded?
options: It measures multi-step grade-school math reasoning
It measures broad factual knowledge across 57 academic subjects
It measures functional Python code-generation ability, graded by actually executing the generated solution against unit tests
It measures commonsense reasoning, graded by human annotators reading the code
questions.explain: HumanEval presents a function signature and docstring, and grades the generated solution by executing it against unit tests -- measuring whether the code actually works, not just whether it looks plausible.

questions.q: Why is reporting a single benchmark score in isolation considered a red flag for an honest evaluation?
options: Because benchmarks are never useful under any circumstances
Because each benchmark targets a specific, narrow capability -- a high MMLU score says nothing about code generation, and vice versa -- so one number doesn't characterize a model honestly
Because only HumanEval is a valid benchmark for any model
Because benchmark scores are randomly generated and meaningless
questions.explain: Each benchmark measures a narrow slice of capability; reporting just one in isolation, especially a favorable one, can obscure how the model performs on everything else, which is why it's often a sign of cherry-picking.

questions.q: What does it mean for a benchmark to be 'saturated,' and why does this reduce its usefulness?
options: A saturated benchmark is one where most competitive models score close to the maximum, so remaining score differences become noise rather than meaningful capability gaps
Saturation means the benchmark's questions have no correct answers
A saturated benchmark has too much training data mixed into it and must be discarded entirely
A saturated benchmark is one that has never been used by any research lab
questions.explain: Saturation occurs when top models cluster near the maximum score, at which point the benchmark can no longer meaningfully discriminate between genuinely stronger and weaker models.

questions.q: What is meant by 'format sensitivity' in benchmark evaluation, and why does it complicate cross-paper comparisons?
options: Format sensitivity refers to the file format (JSON vs CSV) the benchmark results are saved in
It means benchmarks must always be run with zero few-shot examples

Scores can shift based on prompt template, answer-choice labeling, and few-shot example count/order, independent of true model capability -- so two reports of 'the same' benchmark aren't always directly comparable
Format sensitivity only affects benchmarks run on CPUs, not GPUs
questions.explain: Details like prompt wording, few-shot count, and answer presentation can shift scores for reasons unrelated to actual capability, meaning benchmark numbers from different evaluation setups aren't a clean apples-to-apples comparison.

questions.q: What is lm-evaluation-harness, and what role does it play in benchmark evaluation?
options: A tool used exclusively for training models, not evaluating them
EleutherAI's standard open-source tool for running benchmark suites like MMLU, HellaSwag, and GSM8K against a model reproducibly
A hardware monitoring tool for GPU temperature during benchmark runs
A proprietary tool that can only be used by one specific AI lab
questions.explain: lm-evaluation-harness is the standard open-source tool from EleutherAI for running benchmark tasks against a model in a reproducible way, handling prompting, scoring, and aggregation.
